title: Choose the visual world for the Pointer dashboard
question: One world for all three apps, first proven on the Overview. The roll assigned The Blue-Pencil Galley. Keep it, take an alternate, take the category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: The Blue-Pencil Galley
options.lineage: typescript galley proofs marked up in editor's blue pencil
options.thesis: The dashboard is a proof sheet: your app's feedback is marginalia, and the margin is where you act.
options.viewport: One sheet with a wide action margin on the end side (right in LTR, left in RTL). Running head: workspace name small, live comment count set largest in tabular figures. Body: a ruled ledger, one line per project, Open / Ready / Completed as proof marks with counts. The margin carries the next action for that line: install, invite, review. Pending approvals are a blue-pencilled marginal note, not a card. Left rail: small-caps nav over hairlines. No stat tiles anywhere.
options.risk: If the proof marks are decorative rather than functional it reads as a stationery theme. The paper world also pulls toward cream and serif; this direction refuses both (cool bond white, one grotesque) and must hold that line.

raised.raise: Hierarchy carried by scale of one face with tiny mono labels; zero ornament.
A persistent you-are-here mark in the rail, and empty states drawn as the ruled lines they will fill, never a centered icon.
Overview numbers get billing: the number that matters is set largest and the rest step down; no equal tiles.
One typed mark vocabulary for every state (status, approval, on/off), never a colored pill alone.
Sections separated by air and one hairline; no card inside a card.
Color is never the sole signal: every status is mark plus label, and dark mode is a light-table negative rather than gray on gray.

options.label: The Review Margin
options.lineage: pull-request review gutters and inline threads
options.thesis: Feedback on a live app is code review; the dashboard borrows the gutter, the thread rail, and the diff's state colors.
options.viewport: Overview as a review queue. A narrow gutter down the start side holds per-project counts like line numbers; each project row expands into its status threads as counts; statuses use diff green, blue and red chips with glyphs. The primary action is a filled green install button in the merge position, top of the queue.
options.risk: This is where most developer dashboards land and it reads as GitHub at a glance; familiarity is the trade, in exchange for instant legibility to your audience.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: Counts as giant glyphs on paper-white, morphing under a slider.
options.viewport: A giant number fills the screen; a slider morphs the grid below it.
options.risk: A slider that reshapes every glyph is noise inside a task console.
options.case: Fuses poorly: admins do not identify with a type specimen, and an axis slider adds nothing to managing a workspace.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone, tiny monospace labels, no ornament.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.thesis: Statuses as sixteen candy step keys under a chase light.
options.viewport: A dark panel with a quartered step row as the page's one line.
options.risk: Playful and loud, which you named as wrong for this tool.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the step row is a timeline you write into, and a workspace has no beat to write; audience and clarity both lose.
options.kept: A persistent 'where now is' indicator and empty states drawn as structured invitation.

options.label: Festival Lineup Sheet
options.thesis: Every metric billed by size on one saturated ground.
options.viewport: Headliner counts span the width; the long tail packs into a justified block at the foot.
options.risk: Billing works for the Overview and collapses on tables, forms and settings.
options.case: Fuses halfway: the Overview could be billed, but the rest of the console has no billing order; clarity loses and the saturated ground fails the quiet-tool brief.
options.kept: Billing: the number that matters is set largest, the rest step down.

options.label: Copy-Shop Zine Interior
options.lineage: photocopied zine pages on coloured stock
options.thesis: One typed column on goldenrod, controls as typed [ ] and [X] cells.
options.viewport: A single typed column on a warm sheet with the heading platen-enlarged off the edge.
options.risk: A mono-only typeface cannot set Arabic; the RTL constraint fails on fact.
options.case: Fuses poorly: monospace-everything has no Arabic face, and coloured stock as territory reads as a fanzine, not a work console.
options.kept: A single typed mark vocabulary for state instead of colored pills.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.lineage: surreal quarry of cut weather blocks
options.thesis: Sections as cut cloud blocks with sky-blue voids between them.
options.viewport: Stacked white blocks with deep blue gaps; stencil caps on tally boards.
options.risk: Volumetric rendering in an admin console costs performance for no task.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in a workspace maps to cutting weather; both axes lose.
options.kept: Deep separation between sections by space, not by boxes.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: theater cyclorama lighting from night to day
options.thesis: Content in horizon bands lit from black through cobalt to white day.
options.viewport: A dark stage; horizon bands stack from dark to light as state changes.
options.risk: Color as time is not the product; a stage in a work tool reads as theater.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a workspace has no dawn; audience and clarity both lose.
options.kept: Color is never the sole signal; labels and patterns carry every state.

canonCard.label: shadcn admin, played straight
canonCard.thesis: The dashboard every modern SaaS ships, executed at Linear and Vercel finish.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, header, a row of stat tiles, tables below, one blue primary button top right: the arrangement you have now, made impeccable.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design, and the 'generic template' feeling you named.
